title: Clefs and transposition
summary: Move melodies by an octave between clefs, and transpose for instruments in B♭, A and F.

provenance.notes: Items drawn from the seeded generators with a teaching-point filter, then fixed. Music and answers come from the rule engine; prompts and feedback are original.

items.prompt: Write this melody an octave lower in the bass clef, keeping the key signature.

music.textAlternative: A four-note melody in the treble clef, G major: C, D, E, C.

hints: Check middle C as a landmark.
Work out the first note in the bass clef, then keep the same shape for the rest.

feedback.correct: Correct: an octave lower, rewritten for the bass clef.

mistakes.wrong-octave: Check the octave: the new version should be exactly one octave higher or lower — not the same pitch, and not two octaves away.
mistakes.wrong-clef: Look at which clef the question asks for — alto and tenor clefs are easy to mix up.
mistakes.wrong-interval: Check the interval given in the question, and count letter names as well as semitones.
mistakes.wrong-direction: Think about the instrument: a B♭ instrument sounds lower than written, so written notes are higher than concert pitch.
mistakes.key-signature-missing: Work out the new key first and write its key signature.
mistakes.accidental-not-adjusted: Accidentals change too. Work out what each altered note is in the original key, then find the same degree in the new key.
mistakes.enharmonic-respelling: That sounds right, but the spelling is wrong. Keep each note the same interval number above its original.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Transpose the key first, then each note, then check accidentals.

items.prompt: Write this melody an octave lower in the alto clef, keeping the key signature.

music.textAlternative: A four-note melody in the treble clef, C major: F, G, F, G.

hints: Avoid writing at the same pitch.
Work out the first note in the alto clef, then keep the same shape for the rest.

items.prompt: This melody is at concert pitch. Write it as it would appear in a part for horn in F, which sounds a perfect 5th lower than written: transpose it up a perfect 5th, with the new key signature.

music.textAlternative: A five-note melody in Eb major: G, A♭, B♭, A♭, G.

hints: Transpose accidentals by degree, not by copying.
First transpose the key: E♭ major up a perfect 5th is B♭ major. Then move every note by the same interval.

feedback.correct: Right notes and the right new key signature.
